chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who delegated the authority of his wife to a man, saying: 'Bear witness that I have delegated the authority of so-and-so to so-and-so,' and he divorces her. Is that permissible for the man? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.فُلاَنَ: So-and-so (a placeholder name for the delegate)
key_terms.يُطَلِّقُهَا: He divorces her (the act of pronouncing divorce)

ai.seo_question: Is a man's divorce valid if he delegates the authority to divorce his wife to another person?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of *tafwid al-talaq* (delegation of divorce), where a husband grants another person the authority to pronounce divorce on his behalf. The Imam’s affirmative response confirms that such delegation, when clearly declared, renders the third party’s pronouncement legally binding, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for managing marital dissolution without the husband's direct utterance.
